summary: Rabbi Tawil discusses the beginning of Shmuel Bet, focusing on David's reaction to the news of Shaul's death from an Amalekite refugee. The class explores the parallels between the deaths of Eli HaKohen and Shaul, David's lamentation for Shaul and Jonathan, and the emotional role of women in national tragedy.
questions: Why was David furious with the Amalekite boy who claimed to have killed Shaul?
How does the death of Shaul parallel the death of Eli HaKohen earlier in Shmuel
What are the different rabbinic opinions regarding what the Book of the Straight refers to?
Why does David instruct the people to learn the song of the bow?
What connection do the rabbis make between the mother of Sisera and the blowing of the Shofar on Rosh Hashanah?
